A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Misviz/Misviz-synth study. All 19 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison of the methods, experiments, tables, and figures.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original model evaluations and manual error analyses on both datasets. Appendices L and N provide classifier uncertainty estimates and results by data source.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, bounding-box localization, an automatic-annotation pilot, and generalization and prompt-sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The DePlot extractor, linter, and TinyChart/TaPas classifier architecture remain. v2 adds a prompt adaptation producing bounding-box coordinates and explanations instead of only misleader labels (Section 5.6, Appendix K). Renaming the classifiers does not establish an architectural change.

E1.justification: Misviz-synth expands from bar, line, and pie charts to include maps and scatterplots, adding the previously excluded discretized-continuous-variable category. Wikipedia/TabFact tables are removed as a stated source. v2 also evaluates localization and chart filtering/annotation on previously unlabeled images (Section 5.6, Appendix G).

E2.justification: Gemini-1.5-Flash and Gemini-1.5-Pro are replaced by Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite in the main comparisons and source-specific results. The GPT, Qwen, InternVL, linter, and classifier comparator families otherwise remain.

E3.justification: The synthetic corpus becomes 57,665 instances, with five splits replacing v1's 93%/2%/5% training/validation/test split (Section 4.3). The main all-model Misviz comparison expands beyond v1's bar/line/pie subset. New protocols include IoU-based localization and a 100-image manual audit. The prompt study's split is ambiguous: Table 12 says validation, whereas Appendix P says test.

E4.justification: v2 adds classifier/linter analyses by chart-type and misleader counts (Tables 9–10), an ablation of prompt definitions and examples (Table 12), and an automatic-annotation feasibility study (Appendix G). The original source-specific analysis and 30-error-per-dataset manual analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The single-run MLLM evaluation and three classifier seeds with mean±standard-deviation reporting remain. v2 additionally assesses bounding-box annotation agreement on 27 shared images using an IoU threshold of 0.4, reporting agreement of 0.81 (Section 3.4). This adds a distinct annotation-reliability assessment.

E6.justification: Substantial results are replaced under revised data and coverage: image-plus-axis synthetic EM changes from 80.4% to 69.5% (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 2), without establishing a same-setting decline. Full-Misviz GPT-o3 EM also changes slightly, from 58.9% to 58.8%. New findings include 13.1% localization IoU, 98% chart-filtering accuracy, and the analyses in Tables 9–10 and 12.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The retained definitions and methodological explanations receive no substantive formal development; the added IoU evaluation is an experimental metric.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and broad conclusions about detector families remain. The synthetic-resource claim changes from 81,814 charts in v1's abstract to 57,665 in v2, adds per-instance plotting code, and expands to all 12 misleader categories.

C2.justification: v1's broad classifier-transfer interpretation becomes explicitly limited to binary classification; v2 concludes that fine-grained misleader classification does not generalize (Section 5.4). New interpretations address chart complexity, multiple misleaders, automatic-annotation failures, and ambiguity between map-related labels (Appendices G and O; Limitations).

D1.justification: v2 documents per-instance Matplotlib code, the localization prompt and annotation procedure, and checkpoint selection requiring F1 improvement on both validation datasets. These selection details are newly disclosed, without establishing a procedural change. v1's statement about 3,500 extra axis-spacing training examples disappears; most optimization and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the two VIA annotation-tool references, removes the TabFact reference, and attributes its localization prompt to the already cited Chen et al. work. The main research positioning remains; publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 polishes language, renames the classifier category, revises parts of the results narrative, and adds annotation, localization, and supplementary-analysis sections. The overall organization and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: v1's two main performance tables are consolidated into v2 Table 2. v2 adds bounding-box examples and a localization-prompt figure, plus three analysis tables. Existing illustrations are largely retained and relocated, with small styling and caption changes within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Broader synthetic chart coverage and targeted sensitivity analyses make v2 more informative, while the binary-only transfer interpretation better qualifies the generalization finding. Newly disclosed model-selection details also help reproducibility. However, Table 8 and Appendix M retain restricted-subset descriptions that conflict with the main comparison, and Table 12 disagrees with Appendix P about the evaluated split. These reporting ambiguities limit the gains.
